new.description: The Rust suite driving the kind by import, before the embedded lock carries it — `tests/it/settings_kind.rs` is the shape. A program declaring the container over a `.mcp.json` that holds `mcpServers` plus an undocumented top-level key: emit round-trips the file byte-faithfully with the residue intact, the member's rollup fingerprint makes a hand edit to any part of the file drift under the root `fresh` clause, and the `mcpServers` entries stay `mcp-server` members rather than becoming the container's fields.

edit.description: An `Mcp` interface, the `mcp` kind, and `mcpDefaultContract`, modeled on `settings` (:1427) and `settingsDefaultContract` (:1454): locus `{ kind: "at", root: ".", glob: ".mcp.json" }` (the spelling `mcpServer` already uses, :535), `format: "json-document"`, `unitShape: "file"`, `registration: []`. `mcpServers` is neither typed nor gated here — it is `mcpServer`'s collection address (:539), exactly the ownership `settings` gives `hooks`; every other key is opaque residue, no `closedKeys()`. `.mcp.json` documents that one key, so the contract is empty by construction, which is the honest encoding `specs/builtins.md` names ('a format that documents almost no contract gets an almost-empty default contract') — re-verify the key set against code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp at pick-up and carry the retrieved date in the kind's own doc comment.

The provider face's two sorted census lists: `Mcp` joins the type exports (:11), `mcp` and `mcpDefaultContract` join the value exports (:28). The root export stays untouched — a built-in reaches an author through this subpath alone (`specs/builtins.md`, opening paragraph).

The import census (:35) and the 'default contracts ride alongside their kinds through the claude-code subpath' case (:239) gain the kind; a new case pins its locus/format/unit-shape/registration facts the way the `mcpServer` case does (:236) and states that the empty contract is a declared design choice, not an omission — `mcpServers` is the collection address, the residue is opaque. The two blanket cases (:63 well-formed arrays, :73 every clause cited) already range over the new export.
Register the new `mcp_kind` module in the integration harness's module list.

summary: The SDK ships `mcp`: a container kind over the committed `.mcp.json`, `mcpServers` left to the mcp-server collection address, every other key opaque residue.

tests.asserts: a program declaring the container over a `.mcp.json` carrying `mcpServers` plus an unknown key emits byte-faithfully, fingerprints the whole file, and keeps its servers as `mcp-server` members
the `mcp` kind and its (empty) default contract export from the claude-code subpath with the documented locus, json-document format, file unit shape and no registration

acceptance: cargo test and `pnpm --dir sdk test` green (strict tsc included), cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --all --check clean.
notes: Decision 0071, the SDK half — the split `settings` took: a2081d84 shipped the SDK kind plus its Rust suite, 9fcf7521 the embedded lock. MCP-KIND-SHIPS-IN-THE-EMBEDDED-LOCK is the filed successor that earns this export its engine-side consumer; adoption here is by import only, so no fixture outside this entry changes yet. scoped at 3070b747
